evidence.title: Federal Reserve Total Assets
evidence.summary: The snapshotted target change was -1.17 percent; it resolved to 'no'.

evidence.title: Fed’s Balance Sheet Drops $667 Billion fr. Peak to $8.3 Trillion, Below Aug 2021, as QT Continues, Bank Panic Support Unwinds | Wolf Street
evidence.summary: This article directly states that the Fed's total assets dropped by $87 billion in June and by $667 billion since the peak in April 2022, reaching $8.298 trillion. It details the continuation of Quantitative Tightening (QT) and the unwinding of bank liquidity support measures, indicating a clear trend of asset reduction. It also mentions the specific reduction in Treasury notes and bonds and MBS.

evidence.title: Monthly Market Wrap: July 2023 - YCharts
evidence.summary: This source, published after the target period but reflecting on July's events, confirms that the Federal Reserve resumed hiking the Target Federal Funds Rate at its July 26th meeting, raising it by 25 basis points to 5.50%. While not directly about asset growth, rate hikes are a tool used in conjunction with QT to tighten monetary policy, which generally leads to asset reduction.

evidence.title: MSD Weekly Market Update: Week Ending July 14, 2023 - Federal Home Loan Bank of New York
evidence.domain: federal home loan bank of new york
evidence.summary: This report, published mid-July, discusses market expectations for a 25 bps hike at the July 27th FOMC meeting, with odds at ~91%. It also notes that the market was repricing expectations for later in the year and 2024, suggesting a 'one last one and done' scenario. This indicates the Fed's continued hawkish stance, which supports ongoing QT and asset reduction.

evidence.title: Job gains slow, but rising wages, low unemployment keep Fed hikes on track
evidence.summary: This article, published early July, highlights that despite fewer job gains than anticipated in June, strong wage growth and a slight drop in unemployment would likely keep the Fed on track to raise interest rates in July. This reinforces the expectation of continued monetary tightening, which includes QT and balance sheet reduction.

evidence.title: Economic Landscape July 2023 | First Commonwealth Bank
evidence.summary: This report from July states that the Fed was widely expected to raise rates again at the July meeting. It discusses the conditions (sticky inflation, resilient labor/spending) that would likely lead the Fed to continue tightening, which implies continued balance sheet reduction through QT.

evidence.title: U.S. Weekly FundFlows Insight Report: Taxable Bond ETFs and Conventional Funds Attract Net Inflows for the Fund-Flows Week | Lipper Alpha Insight | LSEG
evidence.summary: This report, covering the week ending July 12, notes that minutes from the Fed's June policy meeting 'cast a pall over the market, cementing views that the Fed would raise its key lending rate in July and possibly one more time this year.' This strong signal from the Fed's own minutes indicates a commitment to tightening, which includes balance sheet reduction.
